title: Tenali Raman and the Erased Royal Ledger

full_text:
The Chief Accountant of the Royal Treasury, an arrogant official named Govindaswamy, presented his audited annual revenue ledger to King Krishnadevaraya.
The King noticed that the tax collection from the wealthy diamond district of Bellary was listed as only ten thousand gold coins, whereas the district usually generated fifty thousand gold coins!
When questioned, Govindaswamy insisted:
'Maharaj, drought and poor yields reduced the tax collection. The ledger is written in indelible royal oak-gall ink and stamped with the district seal; it has not been altered by a single stroke!'

The King suspected embezzlement, but the calligraphy appeared smooth, uniform, and untouched to the naked eye.
Tenali Raman was summoned to examine the parchment.

Tenali held the palm leaf ledger up against the bright morning sunlight.
He examined the fibers of the paper beneath a high-magnification quartz lens:
Around the number '10,000', the surface of the parchment was noticeably thinner and slightly rougher than the surrounding paper, indicating that the original ink had been carefully scraped away with a fine razor!

Tenali smiled: 'Maharaj, the ink may be erased, but the chemical memory of the paper remains.'

Tenali procured a small vial of diluted tincture of gallic acid mixed with iron sulfate solution, and a soft camel-hair brush.
In the presence of the King and the trembling accountant, Tenali gently brushed the clear liquid across the scraped area of the ledger.

Within three minutes, a miraculous reaction occurred:
The chemical solution reacted with the invisible iron residues that had soaked deep into the parchment fibers from the original ink!
Right beneath the newly painted '10,000', the original, dark, indelible numbers reappeared with absolute clarity:
**50,000 Gold Coins**!

And right beside it, the original signature of the Bellary tax officer became legible!
Govindaswamy had pocketed forty thousand gold coins and scraped the '5' into a '1'!

The accountant shrieked, fell to his knees on the marble floor, and confessed his crime, revealing the hidden gold buried in his garden cellar.
King Krishnadevaraya was awestruck by Tenali’s brilliant forensic chemistry:
'Tenali, thou hast made invisible truth speak through chemical magic!'
The King restored the forty thousand gold coins to the public works fund, dismissed the corrupt accountant, and rewarded Tenali with a gold-embroidered robe of honor.
moral: Criminals who alter official accounts leave physical traces that chemical science easily exposes.
